newsitem.title: TURKEY: Late bid to save Turkish coalition falters.
newsitem.headline: Late bid to save Turkish coalition falters.

text.p: A late bid to save Turkey's Islamist-led government from collapsing ran into trouble at a three-way meeting of party leaders, Anatolian news agency said.

The agency quoted right-wing leader Muhsin Yazicioglu as saying late on Wednesday after the talks that he was reluctant to prop up the coalition until the alliance partners reached accord on the government's future.
"If the two parties don't agree, we will not be keen on joining a government that has an unclear fate," he said.
Yazicioglu, head of the small Grand Unity Party said Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and his ally, Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, had asked him to bring his party of seven MPs into the government.

The alliance has been losing deputies in a row with the secularist army over Islamist activism and is close to becoming a minority administration. Yazicioglu said Erbakan had rejected a call by Ciller at the talks to make her prime minister until elections in spring 1998, two years before they are due.
"Ciller states that an early election atmosphere has been formed in Turkey. As for Erbakan, he says the government can continue until the year 2000," Yazicioglu said.
Ciller on Wednesday suggested holding early polls to clear the political deadlock which has damaged her secularist True Path Party.
The party was to hold a key meeting at 1030 (0730 GMT) on Thursday to debate the government's future.
Ciller is expected to ask her aides at the meeting for the authority to threaten Erbakan with pulling out of the coalition if he does not hand over power to her soon ahead of early polls.

The partners are to swop jobs next year under a power-sharing deal that established their alliance last June but Ciller says she can ward off army pressure on the government better if she takes the top job sooner.
